subject: MRDS where some transects only have a single observer

messages.author: 6d5a0cbd55c34b88
messages.subject: MRDS where some transects only have a single observer
parts:
I'm currently doing an analysis of some mark-recapture distance sampling data for an arboreal mammal. The majority of transects were surveyed by two observers working independently. For these transects it has been straightforward to fit a MRDS model ( point independence variant) using the mrds package in R, with code like this:

ddf.hr<-ddf(method="io", 
            dsmodel=~cds(key="hr", adj.series=NULL, adj.order=NULL, formula=~1), 
            mrmodel=~glm(link="logit", formula=~distance),
            data=detections, 
            meta.data=meta)

Where  detections is a dataframe containing the distance data (2 entries for each animal recording detection or not by observer 1 and 2), and meta is the list of metadata settings for the model fitting process (not shown here). So far, so good. The model works well, and presented no particular difficulties. 

My question is, whether there is a way to incorporate data from some additional transects that were surveyed using the same methods, but only by a single observer. My thinking here is that if the detection process on these transects is equivalent to that for the first observer on a double-observer transect, then such a model should be estimable. However adding single-observer entries to the detections data.frame for animals observed on the single-observer transects (which usually contains two rows for each individual animal recording detection or not by each observer) results in an error message:

Error in process.data(data, meta.data) : 
  number of records for primary observer not equal to number for secondary observer

Is there perhaps a way to trick mrds into estimating the model I have in mind? Or is this either a very bad idea, or something that is not possible for mrds to do?

Regards,

Michael Scroggie

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] MRDS where some transects only have a single observer
parts:
Michael

Thanks for laying out your question clearly.  Unfortunately, I don't know of a way to fool the software into doing what you desire.  There are error traps (as you discovered) to prevent mismatches of unpaired records (records for each observer) from being processed.  I don't think there's a way to circumvent the situation.

messages.author: 9dce01a6123da978
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] MRDS where some transects only have a single observer
parts:
Apologies if I am over-simplifying, but would there be any disadvantage to treating all observer input as independent transects? Granted, the areas being sampled by each of the paired observers overlaps, but this shouldn't matter either for estimating the detection function (the more data the merrier!) or, provided effort is specified correctly, estimating density. And there should be no problem in adding in data from single observer transects. The only reason I can think of for not doing this is if detection efficiency of an observer in a paired transect is materially affected by the presence of their partner observer (e.g. if there is communication between them to during the transect that leads to more animals being detected than would otherwise be the case; or if animals flushed from one transect are sometimes picked up by the observer on the other transect). If there are differences in efficiency between individual observers, I'd have thought this could be accounted for by including observer ID in the model.

Cheers,

Mark

messages.author: 6d5a0cbd55c34b88
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] MRDS where some transects only have a single observer
parts:
Hi Mark, 

Thanks for your suggestion, but I don't think that would work in our case, because g(0) is substantially less than one. The purpose for using the two observers in our surveys is to gather independent detection data for animals along the transect from two observers, and use a mark-recapture component of the model to infer g(0), thereby correcting for non-detection of animals on the line. Of course, if g(0)=1, then you can just treat the two observers as extra effort as you suggested.

Regards,

Michael Scroggie

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] MRDS where some transects only have a single observer
parts:
Hi Michael, hi listfolks,

Interesting question, which I think distills down to: "can I use
multiple detection functions of different types to obtain one abundance
estimate?"

Eric is correct that there's currently no way in mrds/Distance to do
this unfortunately. I'd like to eventually add to mrds/Distance the
ability to build this kind of joint model.

In the meantime I wonder if a simplistic "manual" version of the
functionality I was thinking about would work. At the moment you have an
estimate of abundance from your MRDS study. You could fit a separate
detection function to the single observer observations and then post-hoc
correct them for g(0), assuming the same value that you got in your MRDS
analysis, then average the densities over the two separate analyses
(you'd assume independence and the CV^2 would add). This would make
sense if there were plenty of single observer observations, but if you
don't have many then the detection function and encounter rate
uncertainties for the single observer bit would end up being rather large.

I can think of more advanced versions of the above but they are rather
more involved and might not be worth it if you don't have that many more
observations or are uncomfortable applying the g(0) estimate to these
other observations.

cheers,
--dave

messages.author: 6d5a0cbd55c34b88
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] MRDS where some transects only have a single observer
parts:
Thanks very much for your suggestions David,

I think the ad hoc approach you mention would work fairly well, especially if there were plenty of both double and single observer transects in the dataset, meaning that distance functions could confidently be fitted to the two data types. It might be less suited to situations where a small minority of the available data are single-observer. I'm yet to decide whether this approach will be suitable for my current problem, but it will probably be worth giving it a try. 

Ultimately, I think I might need to come up with a bespoke means of dealing with both these data-types in an integrated manner. I'm currently working on trying to get point-independence MRDS working in JAGs, which I think could then provide a means of  incorporating the single observer transects into the model by virtue of (assumed) shared parameters. This might actually suit the application we are working on quite well, as we also have in mind to include some other data types as well (transect counts without distances). If we can assume some level of commonality in the detection process for observers undertaking all three survey types, I think we might be able to cautiously stitch the likelihoods for everything together.  

I'm very grateful for your suggestions and your work on the mrds package.

Cheers,

Michael.

>>         same methods, but only by a single observer. My thinking here
>>         is that if the detection process on these transects is
>>         equivalent to that for the first observer on a double-observer
>>         transect, then such a model should be estimable. However
>>         adding single-observer entries to the detections data.frame
>>         for animals observed on the single-observer transects (which
>>         usually contains two rows for each individual animal recording
>>         detection or not by each observer) results in an error message:

>>         Error in process.data(data, meta.data) :
>>           number of records for primary observer not equal to number
>>         for secondary observer
>>
>>         Is there perhaps a way to trick mrds into estimating the model
>>         I have in mind? Or is this either a very bad idea, or
>>         something that is not possible for mrds to do?
>>
>>         Regards,
>>
>>         Michael Scroggie

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] MRDS where some transects only have a single observer
parts:
Hi Michael, hi listfolk,

Just a quick note in case it's useful. I've been experimenting with more
complex likelihoods using Nimble, rather than JAGS. The language is
almost identical but writing custom likelihoods (as we need for MCDS/CDS
models) is much easier than in JAGS (no zeros/ones trick) and much faster.

I've put some example code here:
https://gist.github.com/dill/db6d049a504f52f4b414d7769beffbff in case
it's useful. It's for the point transect case with 2 covariates but I
think it gives the general idea of what you can do in these cases that
are not currently covered by the Distance/mrds packages. To be clear
though, we do hope to include these kinds of analyses in the future!

cheers,
--dave

On 02/10/2020 13:02, Michael Scroggie wrote:
> Thanks very much for your suggestions David,
>
> I think the /ad hoc /approach you mention would work fairly well,

> especially if there were plenty of both double and single observer
> transects in the dataset, meaning that distance functions could
> confidently be fitted to the two data types. It might be less suited to
> situations where a small minority of the available data are
> single-observer. I'm yet to decide whether this approach will be
> suitable for my current problem, but it will probably be worth giving it
> a try.
>
> Ultimately, I think I might need to come up with a bespoke means of
> dealing with both these data-types in an integrated manner. I'm
> currently working on trying to get point-independence MRDS working in
> JAGs, which I think could then provide a means of  incorporating the
> single observer transects into the model by virtue of (assumed) shared
> parameters. This might actually suit the application we are working on
> quite well, as we also have in mind to include some other data types as
> well (transect counts without distances). If we can assume some level of
> commonality in the detection process for observers undertaking all three
> survey types, I think we might be able to cautiously stitch the
> likelihoods for everything together.
>
> I'm very grateful for your suggestions and your work on the mrds package.
>
> Cheers,
>
> Michael.
>
>
> On Fri, Oct 2, 2020 at 9:35 PM David Lawrence Miller
> <da...@ninepointeightone.net <mailto:da...@ninepointeightone.net>> wrote:
>
> Hi Michael, hi listfolks,
>
> Interesting question, which I think distills down to: "can I use
> multiple detection functions of different types to obtain one abundance
> estimate?"
>
> Eric is correct that there's currently no way in mrds/Distance to do
> this unfortunately. I'd like to eventually add to mrds/Distance the
> ability to build this kind of joint model.
>
> In the meantime I wonder if a simplistic "manual" version of the
> functionality I was thinking about would work. At the moment you
> have an
> estimate of abundance from your MRDS study. You could fit a separate
> detection function to the single observer observations and then
> post-hoc
> correct them for g(0), assuming the same value that you got in your
> MRDS
> analysis, then average the densities over the two separate analyses
> (you'd assume independence and the CV^2 would add). This would make
> sense if there were plenty of single observer observations, but if you
> don't have many then the detection function and encounter rate
> uncertainties for the single observer bit would end up being rather
> large.
>
> I can think of more advanced versions of the above but they are rather
> more involved and might not be worth it if you don't have that many
> more
> observations or are uncomfortable applying the g(0) estimate to these
> other observations.
>
> cheers,
> --dave
>
>
>
> On 02/10/2020 10:27, Michael Scroggie wrote:
> > Hi Mark,
> >
> > Thanks for your suggestion, but I don't think that would work in our
> > case, because g(0) is substantially less than one. The purpose
> for using
> > the two observers in our surveys is to gather independent
> detection data
> > for animals along the transect from two observers, and use a
> > mark-recapture component of the model to infer g(0), thereby
> correcting
> > for non-detection of animals on the line. Of course, if g(0)=1,
> then you
> > can just treat the two observers as extra effort as you suggested.
> >
> > Regards,
> >
> > Michael Scroggie
> >
> > On Fri, Oct 2, 2020 at 6:25 PM Mark Wilson <mark....@bto.org
> <mailto:mark....@bto.org>

> > <mailto:mark....@bto.org <mailto:mark....@bto.org>>> wrote:
> >
> >     Apologies if I am over-simplifying, but would there be any
> >     disadvantage to treating all observer input as independent
> >     transects? Granted, the areas being sampled by each of the paired
> >     observers overlaps, but this shouldn't matter either for
> estimating
> >     the detection function (the more data the merrier!) or, provided
> >     effort is specified correctly, estimating density. And there
> should
> >     be no problem in adding in data from single observer
> transects. The
> >     only reason I can think of for not doing this is if detection
> >     efficiency of an observer in a paired transect is materially
> >     affected by the presence of their partner observer (e.g. if
> there is
> >     communication between them to during the transect that leads
> to more
> >     animals being detected than would otherwise be the case; or if
> >     animals flushed from one transect are sometimes picked up by the
> >     observer on the other transect). If there are differences in
> >     efficiency between individual observers, I'd have thought
> this could
> >     be accounted for by including observer ID in the model.
> >
> >     Cheers,
> >
> >     Mark
